questions.q:
The Union Cabinet on 24 February 2026 approved renaming the State of Kerala as 'Keralam' through the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026. Consider the following statements about the constitutional route:
1. The change is made under Article 3 and Parliament passes the Bill by a simple majority.
2. The President must refer the Bill to the Kerala Legislature for its views, which are not binding on Parliament.
3. The change must be ratified by at least half of the State Legislatures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 3 lets Parliament alter the name of a State by ordinary law, after the President refers the Bill to the State Legislature; Parliament is free to ignore the views received. State ratification is needed only for amendments touching the federal features listed in Article 368(2), so statement 3 fails.
questions.s: Business Today, 24 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026
questions.h: Art 3 = Parliament decides, State only advises.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Renaming a State such as Kerala to 'Keralam' under Article 3 does not need a constitutional amendment passed under Article 368.
Statement-II: Article 4 declares that laws made under Articles 2 and 3, though they alter the First and Fourth Schedules, are not to be treated as amendments of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Name changes are done by amending the First Schedule, yet Article 4 says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368, so no special majority is needed. Statement-II is therefore the reason Statement-I holds.
questions.s: Business Today, 24 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q:
In February 2026 Opposition MPs gave notice of a resolution to remove the Lok Sabha Speaker, who stated that he would not preside until the notice was resolved. Consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker can be removed only by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
2. At least 14 days' notice must be given of the intention to move the resolution.
3. While the resolution is under consideration the Speaker cannot preside, but may speak and take part in the proceedings.
4. The resolution must be passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 94(c) requires a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, with 14 days' notice, and Article 96 bars the Speaker from presiding while it is pending though he can speak and take part. A two-thirds majority of members present and voting is not the test, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: All India Radio News, 10 Feb 2026; Scroll, Feb 2026
questions.h: 94(c) removes him from office; 96 keeps him out of the Chair meanwhile.

questions.q:
The Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 received the President's assent on 16 February 2026 and clarified that certain earlier labour laws stand repealed through Section 104 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020. Consider the following Acts:
1. Trade Unions Act, 1926
2. Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946
3. Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
4. Payment of Wages Act, 1936
How many of the above Acts were so clarified as repealed through Section 104 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020?
questions.e: The three Acts on trade unions, standing orders and industrial disputes were the ones folded into the Industrial Relations Code. The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 belongs to the wages stream and was subsumed in the Code on Wages, not the Industrial Relations Code.
questions.s: Taxmann, 16 Feb 2026; PRS India, Feb 2026
questions.h: IR Code swallows 1926, 1946, 1947 - wages go to the Wages Code.

questions.q: The Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 1 of 2026) deals with 'trade unions; industrial and labour disputes'. In the Seventh Schedule, this subject falls in
questions.e: Entry 22 of the Concurrent List covers trade unions and industrial and labour disputes, so both Parliament and State legislatures can legislate on it, with Parliament's law prevailing in a conflict under Article 254. That is why a central Code can replace both central and State-level labour enactments.
questions.s: Taxmann, 16 Feb 2026

questions.q:
MeitY notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 on 10 February 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. They mandate prominent labelling of synthetically generated (AI) content.
2. Significant social media intermediaries, defined as those with over 50 lakh registered users in India, must obtain and verify user declarations on whether content is synthetic.
3. The Rules came into force on the date of notification itself, 10 February 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The amendment requires AI labelling and puts the declaration-and-verification duty on significant intermediaries (over 50 lakh users). The Rules took effect on 20 February 2026, ten days after notification, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Hogan Lovells, Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, 12 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, the time allowed for taking down illegal content flagged by the government or a court was cut to 3 hours from 36 hours.
Statement-II: The Rules were framed under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The takedown window was indeed shortened to 3 hours. The Rules amend the IT Rules, 2021, which are made under the Information Technology Act, 2000, and Section 79 safe harbour is the lever behind them; the DPDP Act, 2023 is a separate data-protection law.
questions.s: Hogan Lovells, Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, 12 Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Report of the 16th Finance Commission was tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was chaired by Arvind Panagariya.
2. Its recommendations cover the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.
3. It recommends retaining the States' share of the divisible pool of central taxes at 41 per cent.
4. It was set up by an Act of Parliament under Article 280.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 match the report. A Finance Commission is a constitutional body that the President constitutes every five years under Article 280, not a body created by an Act of Parliament; Parliament only fixes qualifications and powers by law.
questions.s: PRS India, Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q: Under the Constitution, which Article requires the President to cause every recommendation of the Finance Commission, together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken, to be laid before each House of Parliament? (The 16th Finance Commission's report was tabled on 1 February 2026.)
questions.e: Article 281 is the laying provision. Article 280 constitutes the Commission, Article 275 provides grants-in-aid to States on its advice and Article 282 allows discretionary grants by the Union or a State.
questions.s: PRS India, Feb 2026

questions.q:
On 16 February 2026 a Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant listed the Sabarimala review reference for final hearing before a nine-judge Constitution Bench from 7 April 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The reference is to be finally heard by a Constitution Bench of nine judges.
2. Article 25(2)(b) allows the State to provide for throwing open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus.
3. Article 26 protects the rights of individuals only and not those of religious denominations.
4. The freedom under Article 25 is available only to citizens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The reference concerns Articles 25 and 26, including the meaning of 'sections of Hindus' in Article 25(2)(b). Article 25 is available to all persons, not just citizens, and Article 26 is specifically a right of religious denominations or sections thereof to manage their own affairs in religion.
questions.s: ETV Bharat, 16 Feb 2026; Supreme Court of India listing, Feb 2026

questions.q: On 23 February 2026 the Supreme Court allowed WhatsApp and Meta to withdraw their stay applications after WhatsApp undertook to comply with NCLAT-directed user-consent and data-sharing measures by 16 March 2026. The main appeal that remains pending in the Supreme Court is against a penalty of Rs 213.14 crore imposed by which body?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.e: The Competition Commission of India penalised WhatsApp in November 2024 for abuse of dominance through its 2021 privacy policy. SEBI regulates securities, TRAI telecom tariffs and services, and the RBI banking and payments, so none of them issued this penalty.
questions.s: Bar & Bench, 23 Feb 2026

questions.q:
On 26 February 2026 the Supreme Court, acting on its own cognisance, banned circulation of NCERT's Class 8 Social Science textbook containing a chapter on 'Corruption in the Judiciary'. Consider the following statements:
1. The Court took suo motu cognisance of the matter.
2. It ordered seizure of physical copies and removal of digital versions of the book.
3. It directed the CBI to register an FIR against the NCERT director.
4. It held that NCERT has no power to publish school textbooks.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Court acted suo motu and ordered seizure and takedown, and issued show-cause notices to the NCERT director and the school education secretary. It did not direct a CBI FIR nor question NCERT's authority to publish textbooks.
questions.s: Careers360, 26 Feb 2026; LiveLaw, 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: In State Bank of India v. Union of India (the Aircel and Reliance Communications appeals), the Supreme Court held that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code should be the guiding principle for restructuring ownership and control of telecom spectrum.
Statement-II: Spectrum is a natural resource that the State holds as a trustee for the people, as the Supreme Court recognised in the 2G case (2012).
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Atul S. Chandurkar held the opposite of Statement-I: the IBC cannot be the guiding principle for restructuring ownership and control of spectrum. Statement-II is a correct, settled principle (Centre for Public Interest Litigation, 2012), but it is a separate point, so the answer turns on Statement-I being wrong.
questions.s: Verdictum, 13 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, 16 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Seva Teerth in New Delhi on 13 February 2026, along with Kartavya Bhavan-1 and 2. Which of the following are housed in the Seva Teerth complex?
1. Prime Minister's Office
2. National Security Council Secretariat
3. Cabinet Secretariat
4. Lok Sabha Secretariat
questions.e: Seva Teerth is the integrated executive complex for the PMO, the NSCS and the Cabinet Secretariat. The Lok Sabha Secretariat is a legislative body under the Speaker and is not part of it.
questions.s: PMO India, 13 Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Union Government, the Nagaland Government and the Eastern Nagaland People's Organisation (ENPO) signed a tripartite agreement in February 2026 to create the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (FNTA). Consider the following statements:
1. The agreement was signed among the Centre, the State Government and the ENPO.
2. The FNTA covers the whole of Nagaland.
3. Under Article 371A, an Act of Parliament on Naga customary law applies in Nagaland only if the State Legislative Assembly so decides by a resolution.
4. The FNTA is meant to replace the separate-State demand that the ENPO had raised since 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The FNTA is for six eastern districts, not all of Nagaland, and it substitutes for the ENPO's separate-State demand. Article 371A gives Nagaland special protection, so Parliament's Acts on Naga customary law, religious or social practices apply only if the Assembly resolves so.
questions.s: The Wire, Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Union Cabinet approved the Urban Challenge Fund of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme funded wholly by the Union Government.
2. It carries central assistance of Rs 1 lakh crore for FY2025-26 to FY2030-31.
3. The Centre meets 25 per cent of project cost, and cities must raise at least 50 per cent from the market.
4. Its funds can be used to replace the mandatory State share in all Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are as approved. The Fund is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, which means the cost is shared between Centre and States or other partners, unlike a Central Sector Scheme which the Centre funds fully. Statement 4 has no basis in the approval.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 16 Feb 2026; All India Radio News, Feb 2026

questions.q:
A Ministry of Home Affairs protocol dated 28 January 2026 and publicised in February 2026 governs the playing of the national song. Consider the following statements:
1. The full six-stanza official version of 'Vande Mataram', lasting about 3 minutes 10 seconds, is to be played at official events.
2. Where both are played, 'Jana Gana Mana' must come before 'Vande Mataram'.
3. Dr Rajendra Prasad declared on 24 January 1950 that 'Vande Mataram' would have equal status with the national anthem.
4. 'Vande Mataram' was first published in the journal Bangadarshan in 1875.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The protocol puts the full version first when both are played, so statement 2 reverses the order. Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's song appeared in Bangadarshan in 1875 and was later included in Anandamath in 1882, and the Constituent Assembly's President gave it equal status on 24 January 1950.
questions.s: SCC Online, 12 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q:
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes celebrated its 23rd Foundation Day in February 2026, having been separated from the combined SC/ST Commission on 19 February 2004. Consider the following pairs:
1. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes : Article 338A
2. National Commission for Scheduled Castes : Article 338
3. National Commission for Backward Classes : Article 340
4. Finance Commission : Article 281
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The 89th Amendment (2003) inserted Article 338A and split the joint Commission, leaving Article 338 for the Scheduled Castes. The NCBC derives constitutional status from Article 338B (102nd Amendment), as Article 340 only provides for a commission to investigate backward classes, and the Finance Commission is under Article 280, since Article 281 only lays its report.
questions.s: Vajiram & Ravi, 20 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026
questions.h: 338 SC, 338A ST, 338B BC - A, B, C in order.

questions.q:
The e-Railway Claims Tribunal (e-RCT) system was launched on 27 February 2026 as reform number four under Indian Railways' '52 Reforms in 52 Weeks'. Consider the following statements:
1. It digitises filing, case tracking and document management across the Tribunal's 23 benches.
2. It is part of the '52 Reforms in 52 Weeks' initiative of Indian Railways.
3. It covers only the principal bench of the Tribunal at Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The e-RCT is a nationwide system across all 23 benches, so confining it to the Delhi principal bench is wrong. The Railway Claims Tribunal itself was set up under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987.
questions.s: Vajiram & Ravi, 27 Feb 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q:
A private member's Constitution (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha by P. Wilson on 6 February 2026, proposing proportional representation for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women in higher-judiciary appointments. Consider the following statements:
1. The Bill proposes proportional representation for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women in higher-judiciary appointments.
2. A Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed by a majority of the total membership of each House and by two-thirds of members present and voting.
3. Being a private member's bill, it cannot be introduced without the prior recommendation of the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Any Constitution amendment, whoever introduces it, must clear Article 368's special majority in each House. A private member's bill needs no prior recommendation of the President (only certain financial bills do), so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: SCC Online, 4 Mar 2026; Drishti IAS, Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Supreme Court gave the Telangana Assembly Speaker a final three-week deadline to decide Tenth Schedule disqualification petitions against BRS MLAs who defected. Consider the following statements:
1. The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Constitution Amendment Act, 1985.
2. The 91st Amendment, 2003 removed the exception for a 'split' in a legislature party.
3. The Speaker's decision on disqualification is final and immune from judicial review.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment introduced the anti-defection law and the 91st Amendment deleted the split provision, leaving only merger as a defence. In Kihoto Hollohan (1992) the Court made the Speaker's decision subject to judicial review, which is why courts can fix timelines.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 7 Feb 2026

questions.q: The Supreme Court Collegium approved five retired judges as ad hoc judges of the Allahabad High Court to tackle pendency. Such appointments are made under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 224A lets the Chief Justice of a High Court, with the President's previous consent, request a retired judge to sit as an ad hoc judge. Article 128 is the Supreme Court counterpart, Article 223 deals with an acting Chief Justice and Article 222 with transfer of judges.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 5 Feb 2026

questions.q: The Supreme Court observed that several States continue to appoint 'acting' Directors General of Police in violation of its Prakash Singh (2006) judgment. Which one of the following was the Court's direction on selecting a State DGP in that case?
o: Selection from the three senior-most officers empanelled by the UPSC, with a minimum tenure of two years
Selection by the Chief Minister from all IPS officers of the cadre, with tenure fixed by the State Government
Appointment by the Union Home Ministry from Central Armed Police Force officers for a five-year tenure
Appointment by the Governor on the advice of the State Public Service Commission until superannuation
questions.e: The Prakash Singh directions insulated the DGP from political whim by drawing the choice from a UPSC panel and guaranteeing a minimum two-year term. 'Acting' DGPs bypass this, and since Police is a State subject, the Court's directions are the main check.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 7 Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Supreme Court held that the public trust doctrine extends to artificially created water bodies that serve ecological or environmental purposes. Consider the following statements:
1. The doctrine treats the State as a trustee of resources such as air, water and wetlands, not as their absolute owner.
2. The doctrine applies only to naturally formed resources.
3. In India, the Supreme Court applied the doctrine in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ruling widens the doctrine to ecologically useful artificial water bodies, so statement 2 is wrong. The State holds such resources for public use and cannot alienate them for private gain, a principle the Court drew on in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997).
questions.s: Vajiram & Ravi, 20 Feb 2026

questions.q:
The Election Commission announced biennial Rajya Sabha elections for 37 seats across 10 States in February 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Rajya Sabha members from States are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through the single transferable vote.
2. All 250 members of the Rajya Sabha are elected.
3. One-third of its members retire every second year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength at 250, of whom 12 are nominated by the President for expertise in literature, science, art and social service, so not all are elected. Rajya Sabha is a permanent House whose members serve six-year terms with one-third retiring biennially.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 19 Feb 2026
